//: A second, stricter type check. Run with `npm run typecheck:strict`.
tsconfig.json sets noImplicitAny: false, deliberately, so that untyped
JavaScript still being migrated compiles. The cost is that `tsc --noEmit`
passing proves much less than it appears to: a component whose props are
entirely untyped, or whose .map() callback takes an implicit any, reports
zero errors. This file turns that one flag back on so an untyped prop or
callback parameter is an actual failure.
No files are listed, so the `include` is inherited and this checks exactly
the same set the project builds. That matters in two ways: an error here
points at something real, and `--listFilesOnly` can prove the files were
checked rather than silently absent. A clean run against an empty file list
would be worse than no check at all.
Kept as a separate file rather than folded into tsconfig.json because turning
noImplicitAny on globally is a one-way door: it would also apply to src/test,
which tsconfig excludes and which still has untyped JavaScript. Once that is
converted, this can become the real tsconfig and this file can go.
strictNullChecks is deliberately still off. That is the next step and it is
not cosmetic: it surfaces real null-handling bugs, in code that has been
working, and deserves its own commit rather than being bundled into a
migration.
